business_model: Hardware sales (fitness trackers, speakers), one-time-purchase, low recurring-revenue component

historical_evidence.company: Consumer electronics company (formerly AliphCom) making wireless speakers and, from 2011, the UP line of fitness/wellness wearable trackers, backed by a roster of top-tier investors including Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, Khosla Ventures, and Kleiner Perkins.
historical_evidence.market: Fast-growing consumer wearables/fitness-tracking category as of 2014, but already showing signs of maturing competitive structure with a clear, better-resourced category leader.
historical_evidence.team: Experienced consumer-hardware team with a track record of shipping multiple product generations (speakers, then wearables) and raising from elite investors across several rounds.
historical_evidence.product: UP wearable fitness tracker line, competing directly against Fitbit and, by 2014, an entering Apple/Samsung on smartwatch-adjacent functionality — a crowded and rapidly evolving product category.
historical_evidence.execution: Raised $147M in September 2014 at a $3.2B valuation — a very large late-stage raise for a hardware company, suggesting either strong investor conviction or a need for significant additional capital to compete, or both.
historical_evidence.traction: REPAIRED (see benchmark_notes): NPD Group point-of-sale tracking data, reported by MobiHealthNews, covers the 52-week period from early January 2013 through early January 2014 and puts Fitbit at 68% of fitness-tracker retail unit sales, Jawbone UP at 19%, and Nike FuelBand at 10% — a real, dated, methodologically-labeled competitive-share statistic, though its measurement window ends roughly eight months before the September 2014 snapshot rather than coinciding with it. Looser, undated or vaguely-dated claims elsewhere in circulation (e.g., 'roughly 15%' or 'roughly 18%' for Jawbone 'in 2014') could not be traced to a source with a stated measurement period and have been excluded rather than used to corroborate a more dramatic gap.
historical_evidence.financial: No specific revenue or margin figures were found in the contemporaneous sources reviewed for this snapshot; the scale of the raise ($147M) alongside a distant #2 market position is itself a signal worth flagging for Burn Efficiency/Fundraising Readiness analysis.
